text: One is, there's a group of people who think that software building in the future is going to look very much like it does today, which mostly means text editing, formal programming languages, like TypeScript, and Go, and C, and Rust.
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny asks Michael about his vision of 'what comes after code' - essentially how programming will evolve beyond current methods. Michael is explaining why he disagrees with two popular visions for the future of software development. He argues that one camp thinks nothing will change from today's text-based coding, while another camp believes everything will be done through chatbot-style interactions with AI.
text_ko: 한 가지는, 앞으로의 소프트웨어 개발(software building)은 지금과 거의 똑같을 거라고 생각하는 사람들이 있어요. 그들이 말하는 ‘지금과 비슷한 모습’이라는 건 주로 텍스트 편집(text editing)을 하고 TypeScript, Go, C, Rust 같은 형식적인 프로그래밍 언어(formal programming languages)를 사용하는 형태예요.
text_zh: 有一群人觉得未来的软件开发会和现在很像，基本上还是靠文本编辑（text editing）和正式的编程语言（formal programming languages），比如 TypeScript、Go、C、Rust。
text_es: Hay gente que piensa que, en el futuro, el desarrollo de software (software building) se parecerá mucho a como es hoy: básicamente editar texto (text editing) y usar lenguajes de programación formales (formal programming languages) como TypeScript, Go, C y Rust.
key_sentence: One is, there's a group of people who think that software building in the future is going to look very much like it does today.
original_text: One is, there's a group of people who think that software building in the future is going to look very much like it does today, which mostly means text editing, formal programming languages, like TypeScript, and Go, and C, and Rust. And then there's another group that kind of thinks you're just going to type into a bot, and you're going to ask it to build you something, and then you're going to ask it to change something about what you're building, and it's kind of like this chatbot, Slackbot style where you're talking to your engineering department. And we think that there are problems with both of those visions.

vocabulary.definition: Formal programming languages are structured languages used to write computer programs, characterized by a strict syntax and semantics that enable precise instructions for the computer. Examples include languages like TypeScript, Go, C, and Rust.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, formal programming languages are essential for developing software applications, ensuring reliability, maintainability, and scalability of codebases.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'formal' implies a level of rigor and structure that is often contrasted with more informal or scripting languages, making it suitable for complex and large-scale software projects.

vocabulary.definition: Software building refers to the process of developing, compiling, and assembling software applications from source code into executable programs. This encompasses various stages including design, coding, testing, and deployment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech companies, effective software building is crucial for delivering products that meet market demands and user expectations, often involving collaboration among developers, designers, and project managers.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase 'software building' conveys a sense of construction and craftsmanship, emphasizing the systematic approach required to create functional software, as opposed to ad-hoc or unstructured coding practices.

text: And so a world after code, I think that it looks like a world where you have a representation of the logic of your software that does look more like English, you have written down...
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny is asking Michael to elaborate on his concept of 'what comes after code.' Michael is describing his vision where programming evolves from today's complex code syntax to something more human-readable, resembling English or pseudocode. This represents his prediction for how software development will fundamentally change as AI capabilities improve.
text_ko: 그래서 제가 생각하는 코드(code) 이후의 세계는, 소프트웨어(software)의 로직(logic)을 마치 영어 문장처럼 더 자연스럽게 보이게 하는 표현(representation)을 가지고 있고, 그걸 글로 적어 둔 그런 모습이에요...
text_zh: 所以我觉得所谓的“后代码”(world after code)的世界，会是这样：你对软件逻辑的表述更像英文，而且你已经把它写下来了……
text_es: Creo que, en un mundo más allá del código, tendrías la lógica de tu software (software) representada de forma que se parezca más al inglés, algo que tú mismo hayas escrito...
key_sentence: A world after code resembles a high-level logic representation.
original_text: And so a world after code, I think that it looks like a world where you have a representation of the logic of your software that does look more like English, you have written down... You can imagine in [inaudible] form, you can imagine in kind of an evolution of programming language towards pseudocode. You have written down the logic of the software, and you can edit that at a high level, and you can point at that.

vocabulary.definition: The act of depicting or symbolizing something, often through a model or an abstract form. In computing, it refers to how data or information is structured and presented.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, representation is crucial for visualizing data, creating user interfaces, and ensuring that software accurately reflects user needs and business logic.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'representation' can imply a faithful depiction, it may also suggest simplification or abstraction, so it's important to clarify the context in which it is used.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic method of reasoning that follows a set of principles to arrive at valid conclusions. In programming, it refers to the rules that govern the behavior of algorithms and software.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, logic is fundamental in software development, guiding decision-making processes and ensuring that applications function correctly and efficiently.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'logic' often connotes rationality and clarity, it can also imply rigidity; thus, it's important to balance logical reasoning with creativity in problem-solving.

text: I think taste will be increasingly more valuable. And I think often when people think about tastes in the realm of software, they think about visuals, or taste over smooth animations, and coloring things, UI, UX, et cetera on the visual design of things.
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny asks what skills will become more valuable in the future world where coding evolves beyond traditional programming languages. Michael explains that 'taste' - the ability to make good decisions about what should be built - will become increasingly important. He argues that taste applies not just to visual design elements, but also to the underlying logic and functionality of software.
text_ko: 저는 미적 감각의 가치가 점점 더 커질 거라고 생각해요. 그리고 사람들이 소프트웨어(software) 영역에서 미적 감각을 생각할 때 보통 시각적 요소만 떠올려요. 부드러운 애니메이션(animations), 색감, UI·UX(UI, UX) 같은 시각적 디자인 위주로요.
text_zh: 我觉得品味会越来越值钱。而且很多人一提到软件(software)层面的品味，通常只想到视觉(visuals)——比如流畅的动效(smooth animations)、配色、界面(UI)、用户体验(UX)这些外观设计。
text_es: Creo que el sentido estético tendrá cada vez más valor. A menudo, cuando la gente piensa en "gusto" en el mundo del software, lo asocia con lo visual: animaciones fluidas, paletas de color, interfaz de usuario (UI), experiencia de usuario (UX) y, en general, con el diseño visual de las cosas.
key_sentence: Taste will be increasingly more valuable in the realm of software.
original_text: I think taste will be increasingly more valuable. And I think often when people think about tastes in the realm of software, they think about visuals, or taste over smooth animations, and coloring things, UI, UX, et cetera on the visual design of things. And the visual side of things is an important part of defining a piece of software, but then, as mentioned before, I think that the other half of defining a piece of software is the logic of it, and how the thing works.

vocabulary.definition: Having worth or importance; capable of providing significant benefits or advantages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'valuable' often refers to assets, skills, or insights that contribute to a company's competitive edge or profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'valuable' generally denotes positive attributes, it can also imply a need for careful management to maintain its worth.

vocabulary.definition: The art and practice of creating visual content to communicate messages effectively through typography, imagery, color, and layout.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, visual design is crucial for developing user interfaces that enhance user engagement and brand identity.
vocabulary.nuance: Visual design encompasses both aesthetics and functionality, making it essential for creating user-friendly products.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating moving images or visual effects through the manipulation of graphics or illustrations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In software and web development, animations are used to enhance user interaction and improve the overall experience by making interfaces more dynamic.
vocabulary.nuance: While animations can enhance engagement, excessive use may lead to distractions; thus, they should be applied judiciously.

text: And so I think that more and more, being an engineer will start to feel like being a logic designer, and really, it will be about specifying your intent for how exactly you want everything to work.
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny is asking about what skills will be valuable as programming evolves beyond traditional code. Michael is explaining how the role of software engineers will transform - instead of focusing on the technical implementation details ('how'), engineers will focus more on defining the desired outcomes and logic ('what'). He uses the term 'logic designer' to describe this future role.
text_ko: 그래서 점점 더 엔지니어라는 게 논리 설계자(logic designer)처럼 느껴질 것 같아요. 결국에는 모든 것이 정확히 어떻게 작동하길 원하는지에 대한 의도(specifying your intent)를 명확히 하는 일이 될 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得，做工程师会越来越像当逻辑设计师(logic designer)，说到底就是要把你想让一切究竟怎么运作的意图说明白。
text_es: Creo que cada vez más ser ingeniero se parecerá a ser un diseñador lógico (logic designer), y, en realidad, consistirá en especificar con precisión cómo quieres que funcione todo.
key_sentence: Being an engineer will feel like being a logic designer, specifying your intent.
original_text: And so I think that more and more, being an engineer will start to feel like being a logic designer, and really, it will be about specifying your intent for how exactly you want everything to work. It'd be more about the whats, and a little bit less about how exactly you're going to do things under the hood.

vocabulary.definition: The act of clearly defining or stating the details and requirements of a particular task or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, specifying is crucial for ensuring that all stakeholders understand the objectives and requirements of a project, which helps in aligning efforts and resources effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While specifying is often associated with technical documentation, it can also imply a level of precision that is necessary to avoid ambiguity in communication.

vocabulary.definition: The purpose or goal behind an action or decision, often reflecting the desired outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding intent is vital for aligning strategies and ensuring that team efforts are directed towards achieving common objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: Intent carries a connotation of deliberate planning and thoughtfulness, distinguishing it from mere actions that may lack clear purpose.

text: I think that vibe coding right now describes exactly this state of creation that is pretty controversial, where you're generating a lot of coding, you aren't really understanding the details. That is a state of creation that then has lots of problems, you don't really...
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny asks if Michael's vision relates to 'vibe coding' - a controversial programming approach where developers generate code quickly without fully understanding the technical details. Michael explains that while vibe coding represents a new state of creation, it currently has limitations because when you don't understand the underlying implementation, you eventually hit barriers where you can't modify or scale your creation effectively.
text_ko: 지금 바이브 코딩(vibe coding)이라는 표현은 바로 이런 꽤 논란이 되는 창작의 상태를 정확히 설명한다고 생각해요. 많은 코드를 만들어내긴 하는데 세부 사항을 제대로 이해하지 못하는 그런 상태예요. 그런 창작 상태는 여러 문제를 낳고, 결국에는 잘...
text_zh: 我觉得现在所谓的凭感觉写代码（vibe coding）恰好就是在说这种挺有争议的创作状态：你大量产出代码，但并没有真正弄懂细节。这样的创作方式会带来很多问题，你其实并没有把控住细节……
text_es: Creo que la programación basada en la intuición (vibe coding) describe exactamente este estado de creación que ahora mismo es bastante polémico: estás generando mucho código sin entender realmente los detalles. Ese modo de crear luego acarrea muchos problemas; en realidad no terminas de comprender...
key_sentence: Vibe coding describes a controversial state of creation, limited at a certain point.
original_text: I think that vibe coding right now describes exactly this state of creation that is pretty controversial, where you're generating a lot of coding, you aren't really understanding the details. That is a state of creation that then has lots of problems, you don't really... By not understanding the details under the hood right now, you then very quickly get to a place where you're kind of limited at a certain point, where you create something that's big enough that you can't change.

vocabulary.definition: Causing or likely to cause public disagreement or heated debate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a controversial idea or practice can lead to divided opinions among stakeholders, affecting decision-making and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that the subject matter may provoke strong emotional responses or dissent.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is crucial for effective decision-making, as it allows leaders to analyze data and comprehend market trends.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a depth of knowledge and insight, suggesting that mere familiarity with a subject is insufficient for effective application.

vocabulary.definition: Small, specific pieces of information that contribute to a larger picture or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and business planning, attention to details is essential for ensuring accuracy and success in execution.
vocabulary.nuance: While details are often crucial for thoroughness, excessive focus on them can lead to analysis paralysis or distract from broader objectives.

text: We definitely didn't expect to be doing any of our own model development when we started. As mentioned, when we got into this, there were companies that were immediately from the get-go going and just focusing on training model from scratch.
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny asks about the most counterintuitive lesson Michael learned while building Cursor. Michael explains that they initially planned to rely entirely on existing AI models from other companies, believing it would be inefficient to replicate work that had already been done. However, they eventually discovered that custom model development became essential for creating the best user experience, which was unexpected given their original strategy.
text_ko: 처음 시작할 때 우리 스스로 모델 개발(model development)을 하게 될 줄은 전혀 예상하지 못했어요. 말했듯이, 우리가 이 일에 들어왔을 때는 처음부터 바로 모델을 훈련(training models from scratch)하는 데만 집중하는 회사들이 있었어요.
text_zh: 我们一开始根本没想到要自己做模型开发 (model development)。就像之前提到的，我们刚进来时，有些公司一上来就直接专注于从头训练模型 (training models from scratch)。
text_es: Definitivamente no esperábamos estar desarrollando nuestros propios modelos (model development) cuando empezamos. Como mencioné, cuando nos metimos en esto había empresas que, desde el primer momento, se lanzaron y se dedicaron únicamente a entrenar modelos desde cero (training models from scratch).
key_sentence: We didn't expect to focus on model development from the get-go, replicating others' work.
original_text: We definitely didn't expect to be doing any of our own model development when we started. As mentioned, when we got into this, there were companies that were immediately from the get-go going and just focusing on training model from scratch. And we had done the calculation for what it to train before, and just knew that that was not going to be able to do. And also felt a bit like focusing one's attention in the wrong area, because there were lots of amazing models out there, and why develop all this work to replicate what other players had done.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating, refining, and implementing a mathematical or computational representation of a system or phenomenon.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, model development is crucial for data analysis, predictive analytics, and machine learning applications, allowing companies to make informed decisions based on data-driven insights.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a systematic approach and can suggest a level of sophistication in the techniques used, making it more suitable in formal discussions about technical processes.

vocabulary.definition: Concentrating attention or resources on a particular subject, task, or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, focusing on specific goals or areas of improvement is essential for effective resource allocation and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase can imply a deliberate choice to prioritize certain aspects over others, which can be critical in discussions about strategy and operational efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: The process of teaching a machine learning algorithm to recognize patterns in data by adjusting its parameters based on input data and outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups and data-driven companies, training models is a fundamental step in developing applications that rely on artificial intelligence and machine learning, impacting product functionality and user experience.
vocabulary.nuance: This term is often associated with technical jargon in data science, and while it is widely understood in the field, it may require clarification for audiences outside of tech.

text: And at this point, every magic moment in Cursor involves a custom model in some way.
speaker: Michael Truell
context: Lenny asks about counterintuitive lessons from building Cursor. Michael is continuing his explanation about how they unexpectedly ended up developing their own AI models despite initially planning to rely on existing ones. He reveals that every impressive feature ('magic moment') in Cursor now uses some form of custom model, and this transition happened gradually as they found specific use cases where custom models significantly outperformed existing foundation models.
text_ko: 이제는 Cursor에서 일어나는 모든 특별한 순간들이 어떤 식으로든 커스텀 모델(custom model)과 연결돼요.
text_zh: 现在这个阶段，Cursor 里所有让人眼前一亮的时刻，或多或少都离不开定制模型 (custom model)。
text_es: A estas alturas, en Cursor cada momento clave implica, de algún modo, un modelo personalizado.
key_sentence: every magic moment in Cursor involves a custom model in some way.
original_text: And at this point, every magic moment in Cursor involves a custom model in some way. So that was definitely counterintuitive, and surprising, and it's been a gradual thing, where there was an initial use case for training our own model, where it really didn't make sense to use any of the biggest foundation models. That was incredibly successful, moved to another use case that worked really well, and had been going from there.

vocabulary.definition: A tailored framework or system designed to meet specific requirements or preferences, often used in data analysis or software development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, custom models are frequently developed to address unique business challenges or to enhance user experiences through personalization.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'custom model' implies a level of personalization, it is important to ensure that the model is scalable and adaptable for broader applications.
